explain.say: One evening a poor carter, John Durbeyfield, is told he descends from a great Norman family, the d'Urbervilles. That small piece of news sets his daughter Tess on a road to ruin. Thomas Hardy published the novel in 1891. A gentle note: this story includes sexual assault and a death, and we will go carefully.

explain.say: Look at the second and third panels. Sent to claim kinship with rich so-called cousins, Tess meets Alec, who pursues her and, one night in the woods called the Chase, assaults her while she sleeps. Hardy leaves the scene blurred, and critics still argue over the words for it. Why might a Victorian writer have had to blur it?

explain.say: Look at the two sides. On their wedding night Angel confesses a past affair, and Tess forgives him at once. Then she tells her story, and he leaves her. This is the double standard: one moral rule for men, a harsher one for women. Hardy's subtitle calls Tess a pure woman, a direct challenge to his readers. Was Angel fair?

explain.say: Why is Tess destroyed? Hardy piles up reasons: chance, like the confession letter that slips under a carpet unread; poverty; a society that blames the victim; and a universe that does not care. People call this Hardy's fatalism, the sense that fate is stacked against you. Which reason feels strongest to you?

explain.say: Alec returns when her family is homeless, and Tess becomes his mistress. When Angel comes back, she kills Alec, flees with Angel for a few days, and is arrested at dawn at Stonehenge, then hanged. Well done for staying with a hard story. Challenge: Hardy says the President of the Immortals had ended his sport with Tess. Whom is he blaming?

faq.a: Hardy leaves the scene in the Chase ambiguous, partly because Victorian editors would not print it plainly. Many modern critics read it as rape, since Tess is asleep and has already refused Alec; the novel insists she is not to blame.
asks: What happens to Tess in the Chase?

faq.a: When she tells him about Alec and her baby, he cannot forgive her, though he has just confessed his own affair and she forgave him. He sees her as a different woman and goes to Brazil.
asks: Why does Angel Clare reject Tess?

faq.q: What happens to Tess at Stonehenge?
faq.a: After killing Alec, Tess flees with Angel. They rest at Stonehenge, she sleeps on an ancient stone, and police arrest her at dawn. She is hanged at Wintoncester.

faq.q: Why did Hardy call Tess a pure woman?
faq.a: His subtitle, A Pure Woman Faithfully Presented, argues that purity lies in intention and character, not in what was done to her. It provoked many Victorian readers.
asks: What does A Pure Woman Faithfully Presented mean?

faq.a: Hardy's name for his fictional version of south-west England, based mostly on Dorset and nearby counties, where his novels are set. He took the name from an old Anglo-Saxon kingdom.

facts: Tess of the d'Urbervilles was published in 1891, after a cut version ran in the newspaper The Graphic.
Its subtitle is A Pure Woman Faithfully Presented.
Hardy's Wessex is based mainly on Dorset in south-west England.
